basis: praise as the creature's response to its maker
note: The commentary places hamd before naming the specific gift; Augustine opens by praising God as creator and says human beings are made for God, so praise is the fitting response to dependence itself.
Didache yaşam yolu ile ölüm yolunu karşı karşıya koyar; 1:7'deki toplulukların ayrılan yollarına erken Hristiyan etik köprü kurar.

basis: thanksgiving for gifts of knowledge and life
note: The commentary says praise follows what God gives; after the meal the community thanks the holy Father for his name, knowledge, faith, and immortality given through Jesus.

basis: food given so people may thank the creator
note: The commentary says recipients answer God's provision with hamd; the post-meal prayer says God gave food and drink to humanity so that people might thank him, then names the community's spiritual food and drink.

basis: the prayer ends in glory to God
note: The commentary says the opening hamd returns at the end of the path; the Didache's thanksgiving closes by ascribing glory to God forever.
Didache verirken tereddüt etmemeyi ve homurdanmamayı söyler; armağanı alıcıya serzeniş yapmama yönünde erken Hristiyan etik paraleldir.
The commentary makes hamd the recipient's response to a gift; the community's meal prayer gives thanks over the cup and broken bread as gifts from God through Jesus.

basis: gathering the Church as one people
note: The commentary says favor belongs to a community and its path; the Eucharistic prayer asks that the scattered Church be gathered into God's kingdom, like bread once scattered and made one.

basis: thanks for grace given in Christ
note: The commentary makes praise the response to a received gift; Paul thanks God for grace given to the Corinthian believers in Christ.

basis: God sustains believers to the end
note: The commentary links a completed favor to a walked path; Paul says Christ will strengthen the community to the end, blameless at his day.

basis: work attributed to grace rather than self
note: The commentary warns against presenting one's own effort as a merit; Paul says he worked hard, yet attributes what he is and his work to God's grace.

basis: what was received leaves no ground to boast
note: The commentary warns against advertising what one spent as one's own merit; Paul asks what anyone has that was not received and rejects boasting as though it were not received.
Her şeyi almış olanın, almamış gibi övünmemesi, nimeti kendi başarı ya da başkasına karşı üstünlük diye göstermeyi tersine çevirir.

basis: received goods shared with a brother
note: The commentary's hand-to-hand image traces good from giver to recipient; John asks how God's love can remain in someone who sees a needy brother and closes the heart despite possessing the world's goods.

basis: love enacted rather than merely spoken
note: The commentary contrasts genuine praise and giving with words that claim merit; John requires love in deed and truth, giving the response a practical form.

basis: love as a response to prior love
note: The commentary makes the recipient's response follow the giver's favor; John says believers love because God first loved them.

basis: blessing God for new birth and hope
note: The commentary makes hamd the answer to a favor; Peter blesses God for new birth to a living hope through Jesus' resurrection.
Tanrı bereketlenir; büyük merhametine göre yeniden doğuş vermiştir: hamd ile ihsanın kaynak-sonuç dizilişidir.
The commentary says the favor belongs to a community and its path; Peter names an imperishable inheritance kept in heaven for believers.

basis: faith tested toward praise and honor
note: The commentary makes the path end in a completed favor; Peter says tested faith will result in praise, glory, and honor at Jesus' revelation.

basis: once not a people, now recipients of mercy
note: The commentary identifies a community by the favor it received; Peter says those once outside the people have become God's people and have received mercy.

basis: called from darkness to proclaim praises
note: The commentary asks for the path of people favored by God; Peter describes a people called from darkness into marvelous light to proclaim God's excellencies.
Seçilmiş topluluğun kendisini karanlıktan ışığa çağıranın erdemlerini ilan etmesi, lütfu başkalarına sayan ortak hamddir.

basis: stewarding a gift for one another
note: The commentary pictures favor as good delivered to another; Peter tells each person to use the gift received to serve others as a steward of God's varied grace.
Herkes aldığı armağanı birbirine hizmet etmekte kullanır; iyiliğin bir elden ötekine ulaştırılması olarak in‘âmın cemaat içi biçimidir.
Tanrı'nın yarattığı her iyi şeyin şükranla kabul edildiğinde reddedilmemesi, rızka verilen açık Hristiyan teşekkür cevabıdır.

basis: riches are gifts, not grounds for pride
note: The commentary rejects self-credit for what one has received; Paul tells the rich not to be arrogant but to hope in God, who richly provides all things to enjoy.
Tanrı'nın zevk almak için her şeyi bolca sağladığı sözü, en‘ame'nin fazlasını verme ve artırma yönüne açık fakat anlatısız bir karşılıktır.

basis: received wealth used generously for others
note: The commentary depicts good passing from hand to hand; Paul tells the wealthy to do good, be generous, and ready to share.
The commentary names mercy as the source of good; Paul blesses the Father of mercies and God of all comfort.
Bereket formülü Tanrı'yı merhametlerin Babası ve her tesellinin Tanrısı diye över; rahmetin iyilik kaynağı oluşunu Hristiyan doxolojisine taşır.

basis: comfort received and passed to others
note: The commentary pictures beneficence moving from giver to recipient; Paul says God comforts believers so they can comfort others in the trouble they themselves have received comfort through.

basis: grace multiplying thanksgiving to God's glory
note: The commentary says the recipient's praise follows God's favor; Paul says grace reaching more people multiplies thanksgiving to God's glory.
Lütuf daha çok kişiye yayıldıkça şükranın Tanrı'nın yüceliğine çoğalması, verilen iyiliğin başkaları arasında hamde dönüşmesiyle örtüşür.
Titus'tan, başlattığı χάρις yani bağış toplama iyiliğini tamamlaması istenir; bu, iyiliğin sonuna kadar yapılması motifidir.
The commentary says the giver's good reaches a recipient who praises; Paul says generosity enriches the giver and produces thanksgiving to God through the recipients.
Her cömertlik için her bakımdan zenginleştirilmek, elçiler aracılığıyla Tanrı'ya şükran doğurur; artırılmış nimet ile hamdin zinciridir.
The commentary links conveyed good with praise of its source; Paul says the service supplies the saints' needs and overflows in many thanksgivings to God.
The commentary depicts beneficiaries recounting the giver's good; Paul says recipients glorify God for the donors' confession and generous sharing.
The commentary says praise answers a gift; Paul closes the account of giving by thanking God for his inexpressible gift.
Tanrı'nın tarif edilemez armağanına şükür, bağış karşısındaki doğrudan cevap olarak durur.
The commentary's B010 branch says giving may exceed what is sufficient; Paul says God can make grace abound so believers have sufficiency for every good work.

basis: lütfun çoğalması ve her iyi iş
note: Tanrı lütfu bol bol artırır ki alıcılar her iyi iş için yeterli olsun; yorumdaki en‘ame “artırdı” ile tamamlanan ihsanı tek bağlamda tutar.

basis: divine power grants what leads to life
note: The commentary joins bestowed favor with a path to walk; Peter says God's power has granted everything needed for life and godliness, calling believers by glory and excellence.

basis: food, gladness, and witness to God's goodness
note: The commentary connects divine favor to the provision of good; Paul says God gave rain, fruitful seasons, food, and gladness, leaving witness among the nations.
Tanrı'nın iyilik yapıp yağmur, verimli mevsimler ve yiyecekle doyurması, 106:3–4'teki besleyen Rabbe kamusal elçi tanıklığıdır.

basis: God gives life and breath to all
note: The commentary describes the giver as the source of good; Paul says God is not served as though needy, since he himself gives all people life, breath, and everything.

basis: hayat, soluk ve her şeyi veren
note: Her insana hayatı, soluğu ve her şeyi veren Tanrı, 1:2'deki bütün âlemlerin Rabbine evrensel sağlayıcı olarak karşılık verir.
İsa'ya atfedilen vermenin almaktan daha bereketli olduğu sözü, yorumun elden ele geçen iyilik imgesine belirgin ama daha genel bir etik paralel sağlar.

basis: the healed man walks and praises God
note: The commentary joins a received favor to its path and response; the healed man enters the temple walking and leaping while praising God.

basis: the public sees the recipient praising
note: The commentary says the beneficiary can voice praise before others; everyone sees the formerly lame man walking and praising God.
Firavun'un soya kötü davranıp bebekleri ölüme bırakması, sarayda büyütülmeyi lütuf sayan sözün baskı politikasıyla gerilimini Hristiyan anlatıda da kurar.

basis: Pharaoh's daughter takes Moses as her son
note: The commentary places the claim of raising Moses in Pharaoh's mouth; Stephen's retelling attributes his rescue and adoption to Pharaoh's daughter, preserving the household upbringing but changing the agent.
Stefanus, terk edilen Musa'nın Firavun'un kızı tarafından alınıp kendi oğlu gibi yetiştirildiğini söyler; 26:18–22'nin yetiştirme sahnesinin Hristiyan yeniden anlatımıdır.

basis: thanks for a share in the inheritance
note: The commentary says a community receives a path and a gift; Paul gives thanks to the Father who qualified believers to share in the inheritance of the saints in light.

basis: transfer from darkness into a kingdom
note: The commentary contrasts the favored path with those astray; Paul says God rescued believers from the authority of darkness and transferred them into the Son's kingdom.
The commentary says favor is completed by walking its path; Paul tells believers to walk in Christ Jesus, whom they received.
The commentary joins the path of favor to praise; Paul describes believers as rooted and built up in Christ, abounding in thanksgiving.
Mektup Tanrı'yı kutsayarak açılır ve onun bizi ruhsal bereketlerle bereketlediğini söyler; Fâtiha'nın nimet adından önce hamdi getiren düzenine yakındır.
The commentary says the favor is completed by walking the path; Paul says God made believers for good works prepared for them to walk in.
Tanrı'nın önceden hazırladığı iyi işlerde yürümek üzere yaratılma, bağışlanan lütuf ile yolun birlikte yaşanmasıdır.
The commentary says the path is a favor received from God; Paul describes salvation as grace through faith and God's gift.

basis: no boasting in one's own works
note: The commentary rejects claiming one's own expenditure as a favor; Paul excludes boasting because salvation is not from works.
Pavlus, “sende bütün uluslar bereketlenecek” sözünü İbrahim'e önceden müjde diye okur; seçilmiş ve bereketlenen İbrahim için belirgin Hristiyan yorum köprüsüdür.

basis: tek sunuyla sonsuza dek yetkin kılmak
note: Mesih'in tek sunusunun kutsananları sonsuza dek yetkin kıldığı iddiası, 5:3'te dinin tamamlanmasına ilişkin Kur'anî ifadeyle farklı bir Hristiyan tamamlama anlatısı kurar.

basis: Moses refuses the status of Pharaoh's daughter's son
note: The commentary presents a royal upbringing invoked as a favor; Hebrews says Moses later refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter, emphasizing his break with that household identity.

basis: praise voiced as the fruit of lips
note: The commentary says the recipient should recount the benefactor's good; Hebrews calls believers to offer continual praise to God, the fruit of lips that confess his name.

basis: her iyi şeyle donatıp iradeyi yapmak
note: Tanrı'nın iradesini yapmak için her iyi şeyle donatması ve içeride işlemesi, Rabbin iyiliği tamamlama ve düzene koyma işlevine Hristiyan karşılıktır.

basis: every good gift comes from above
note: The commentary says all good reaches the recipient from its giver; James says every good giving and perfect gift comes down from the Father of lights.
Her iyi bağış ve her tam armağan yukarıdan iner; nimet, veren ve tamlık aynı cümlede yorumun en‘ame ile geliştirdiği tamamlanma çağrısıyla buluşur.
The commentary says a gift can be ruined by holding it over its recipient; James says God gives wisdom generously to all and does not reproach the one who asks.
Tanrı isteyen herkese cömertçe ve ayıplamadan verir; hem ihsanın serbestliği hem de başa kakmamanın açık karşıtıdır.

basis: fullness received as grace upon grace
note: The commentary's secondary gloss says a gift may be increased beyond measure; John says all received from Christ's fullness, grace upon grace.
Fâtiha Tanrı'dan yola iletmesini ister; bu ayet İsa'nın kendisini Baba'ya giden yol diye tanıtır. Aynı yol iddiası farklı bir Hristiyan kurulum alır.
İbadetin ne bu dağda ne de Yeruşalim'de yapılacağı saat, kıblenin yüzü eve döndürmesiyle aynı kutsal yön meselesine farklı Hristiyan cevap verir.
Gerçek tapınanların Baba'ya Ruh ve hakikatte tapınması, yer-yön merkezli ibadete dair bir önceki ayetin olumlu Hristiyan karşı anlatısıdır.
The commentary says praise answers a gift and its B010 gloss includes giving more; Jesus gives thanks, distributes the loaves, and feeds the crowd.
İsa ekmekleri alır, şükreder ve oturanlara diledikleri kadar dağıtır; veren el, doyurma ve şükür aynı sahnede birleşir.
The commentary says anʿama can mean adding beyond enough; after the crowd is filled, Jesus orders the surplus fragments gathered so none is lost.
The commentary asks for a path that does not stray; Jude praises God who is able to keep believers from stumbling and present them blameless.

basis: glory to the only God at the journey's end
note: The commentary says the opening praise returns at the end of the path; Jude's closing doxology gives glory, majesty, power, and authority to God through Jesus Christ.

basis: Mary magnifies God in response to favor
note: The commentary says the receiver answers a gift with praise; Mary publicly magnifies the Lord and rejoices in God her savior.

basis: God has done great things for Mary
note: The commentary's hamd recounts the giver's good; Mary says the Mighty One has done great things for her and names his holiness.
Meryem, Kudretli'nin kendisi için büyük işler yaptığını yüceltici bir ilahide söyler; alıcının nimetini hamd içinde ilan etmesidir.
The commentary presents mercy as the source of blessing; Mary says God's mercy extends from generation to generation to those who fear him.

basis: God raises the lowly and brings down rulers
note: The commentary distinguishes those given favor from the contrary way; Mary's song describes God reversing status by bringing rulers down and exalting the lowly.
The commentary says favor is a gift delivered to recipients; Mary sings that God fills the hungry with good things and sends the rich away empty.
Tanrı'nın kul İsrail'e yardımının merhameti hatırlaması olarak anlatılması, 12:6'daki haneye ve atalara uzanan nimete Hristiyan ilahi paralelidir.
The commentary makes hamd the answer to received favor; Zechariah begins by blessing Israel's God for visiting and redeeming his people.
Zekeriya, Tanrı halkını ziyaret edip kurtardığı için “kutsansın” diyerek ilahi iyiliğin övgüye dönüşmesini anlatır.
The commentary connects the path of the favored to divine mercy; Zechariah says the redemption enacts mercy promised to the ancestors and remembrance of the covenant.
The commentary says mercy is the source of beneficence; Zechariah attributes the coming dawn to the tender mercy of God.
Tanrı'nın şefkatli merhameti yüzünden yukarıdan doğan ışık ziyaret eder; 1:1 ve 1:3'teki rahmetin hidayete kaynak olmasıyla birleşir.

basis: guiding feet into the way of peace
note: The commentary joins received favor to a path; Zechariah says the dawn will guide feet into the way of peace.
Bu ziyaretin işi ayakları esenlik yoluna yöneltmektir; nimet ile yol gösterme bağı için doğrudan İncil paralelidir.

basis: the healed man glorifies God aloud
note: The commentary says the recipient recounts the giver's favor; one healed leper returns, loudly glorifying God.
İyileşen Samiriyeli geri dönüp yüksek sesle Tanrı'yı yüceltir; nimet alıcısının hamd cevabını gösterir.
The commentary makes hamd the recipient's answer to a gift; the Samaritan falls at Jesus' feet and thanks him after healing.
Aynı kişi İsa'nın ayaklarına kapanıp teşekkür eder; yanındaki yüceltme ile teşekkürün ayrı eylemler oluşu, hamd ile şükrün geniş-dar ilişkisini düşündürür.

basis: the foreigner returns to praise God
note: The commentary says praise of the benefactor should be voiced; Jesus asks whether only the foreigner returned to give glory to God.
The commentary distinguishes praise of the giver from claiming one's own merit; the Pharisee thanks God while boasting that he is unlike other people.

basis: the self-exalting and humble are reversed
note: The commentary contrasts benefactor-praise with self-praise; Jesus says the self-exalting Pharisee is not justified, while the humble tax collector is.
Ulusların kralları egemenlik sürer ve yetkililer “iyilik yapanlar” diye anılır; Firavun'un yetiştirme iyiliğini iktidar diliyle başa kakmasına eleştirel bir siyasi karşılıktır.
The commentary says mercy is the source of beneficence; Jesus describes God as kind even to the ungrateful and evil, then commands love of enemies.
Düşmanlara iyilik edip geri ödeme ummadan ödünç verme buyruğu, iyiliği alıcı üzerinde alacak veya üstünlük aracına çevirmemeyi Tanrı'nın iyiliğine bağlar.
The commentary presents receiving God's mercy as the ground of a favored way; Jesus tells disciples to be merciful as their Father is merciful.
İsa, iyileşene evine dönüp Rabbin ona ne yaptığını ve nasıl merhamet ettiğini anlatmasını emreder; 93:11'de nimeti anlatma emrine doğrudan karşılıktır.

basis: freely received good freely passed on
note: The commentary pictures favor passing from hand to hand; Jesus tells disciples that what they received freely they should give freely as they heal and proclaim.
İsa'nın “Sana hamd ederim, Baba, göğün ve yerin Rabbi” hitabı, hamd fiilini 1:2'nin evrensel Rab hitabıyla birleştirir.
The commentary pictures good passing from one hand to another; the king has compassion and cancels a servant's debt, a received favor that sets up the servant's obligation toward another.

basis: failure to pass received mercy onward
note: The commentary says an act of kindness is carried to another; the king condemns the forgiven servant for failing to show his fellow servant the mercy he received.

basis: Rabbin yolunu hazırlamak ve yolları düz kılmak
note: Yahya'nın ilanı Rabbin yolunu hazırlamayı ve yolları düz kılmayı söyler; sırât-ı müstakîm için gelişe hazırlayan bir yol imgesidir.
İsa'nın Yasa ve Peygamberleri kaldırmaya değil yerine getirmeye geldiği sözü, 5:3'teki dinin tamamlanmasıyla karşılaştırılacak bir Hristiyan tamamlama iddiasıdır.

basis: sun and rain given to just and unjust
note: The commentary identifies mercy as the source of good; Jesus says the Father gives sun and rain to both evil and good, extending divine beneficence beyond a single favored group.
Gündelik ekmeğin Baba'dan istenmesi, 106:4'teki rızkın gerçek kaynağına yönelen daha dolaylı bir dua paralelidir.
The commentary distinguishes recounting God's favors from holding one's own generosity over people; Jesus warns that public almsgiving for recognition receives its reward from people.
Sadakayı borazanla duyuranların insanlardan övgü araması, iyiliği başkaları önünde kendine paye yapmakla ilgili Hristiyan uyarıdır.

basis: the giver does not advertise the gift
note: The commentary condemns self-credit for one's spending; Jesus says the giver's left hand should not know what the right hand gives.
The commentary contrasts service with self-praise; Jesus says secret giving is seen and rewarded by the Father.

basis: the broad way leading to destruction
note: The commentary asks for one path and distinguishes its recipients from those astray; Jesus says the wide gate and broad way lead to destruction.

basis: the narrow way leading to life
note: The commentary asks for the path of the favored; Jesus contrasts the narrow gate and hard way that lead to life.
Dar yolun hayata götürmesi ve az kişinin onu bulması, doğru yolun varışını Fâtiha'daki nimetli yol düşüncesiyle buluşturur.
The commentary's B002 gloss on Rabb is completion of beneficence and its path ends in walking; Paul trusts God to complete the good work begun in the believers until Christ's day.
Tanrı'nın başlattığı iyi işi sonuna dek tamamlayacağı vaadi, iyilik/ihsanın yalnız başlanmayıp bitirilmesi için Hristiyan paralelidir.

basis: tamamlanma ve hayat suyunun karşılıksız verilmesi
note: “Tamamlandı” ilanıyla susayana hayat suyunun karşılıksız verilmesi, nimetin tamamlanması, bağış ve son varış temasını tek eskatolojik cümlede toplar.

basis: creatures acknowledge the giver of all things
note: The commentary makes praise the response to God's favor; the heavenly elders worship the creator because all things exist by his will.
Gökte, yerde ve denizde bütün yaratılış tahttakine bereket, onur, yücelik ve kudret verir; âlemlerin Rabbine hamdin kozmik karşılığıdır.

basis: salvation belongs to God and the Lamb
note: The commentary names a community by the favor it received; the multitude cries that salvation belongs to God and the Lamb before the elders' full doxology.

basis: thanksgiving and praise before the throne
note: The commentary places hamd as the fitting answer to God's favor; the heavenly assembly ascribes blessing, glory, wisdom, thanksgiving, honor, power, and might to God.
Taht çevresindeki sözler bereket, yücelik, hikmet ve şükranı Tanrı'ya verir; yolun ve cennetin sonunda dönen hamd için eskatolojik paraleldir.

basis: the Lamb shepherds and guides to water
note: The commentary joins divine favor with a path; the Lamb shepherds the multitude and guides them to springs of living water.
Kuzu onları güdecek, hayat sularının pınarlarına yöneltecek ve Tanrı gözyaşlarını silecektir; yol nimeti ile varıştaki iyiliği birleştirir.

basis: failure to glorify or give thanks
note: The commentary presents praise as the due answer to received good; Paul describes people who knew God yet neither glorified him nor gave thanks.
The commentary warns against self-praise for a favor received; Paul tells grafted-in Gentiles not to boast over the natural branches because the root supports them.

The commentary distinguishes those receiving favor from those under anger; Paul sets God's kindness toward believers beside severity toward those who fell, and warns the former to continue in kindness.

basis: no one first gives to God
note: The commentary says the beneficiary answers a gift with praise rather than claiming merit; Paul asks who has ever given God something first so that God must repay.

basis: all things come from God and return to him
note: The commentary makes the giver's favor the source and goal of the recipient's path; Paul says all things are from, through, and for God, to whom glory belongs.
Mesih'in sünnetlilere hizmetinin atalara verilen vaatleri doğrulamak için olduğu yorumu, Yakup hanesine uzanan nimetin Hristiyan okumasını verir.
The commentary says mercy is the source of the favor that guides a person; Paul says God's kindness, forbearance, and patience lead toward repentance.
Tanrı'nın lütfu kurtuluş getirerek görünür; in‘âmın alınan bir armağan oluşuna Hristiyan karşılıktır.
Aynı lütuf insanları ölçülü, adil ve dindarca yaşamaya eğitir; lütuf sadece verili şey değil, yürünecek yolu biçimleyen güçtür.

basis: salvation from mercy rather than deeds
note: The commentary makes divine mercy the source of favor; Titus says God saved people through mercy, not righteous works they had done.

basis: grace makes recipients heirs in hope
note: The commentary says favor is a gift that carries a community toward its end; Titus says believers justified by grace become heirs according to the hope of eternal life.
Talmud, dışarıdaki kişinin kalbini İsrail'e, Kudüs'e, Mabede ve Kutsallar Kutsalı'na yöneltmesini öğretir; kıblenin ev ve yön görüntüsü için Yahudi ibadet okumasıdır.
Talmud, denizden geçen, çölde yürüyen, hastalıktan çıkan ve hapisden kurtulanın topluluk önünde şükür berekesi söylemesini ister; iyiliği duyurma ve yolun sonunda hamd için somut ritüeldir.
Berakhot, Leah'nın “bu kez YHWH'ye şükredeceğim” sözünü ilk açık teşekkür diye okur; alınan çocuk/nimet karşısında hamdin Yahudi yorum geleneğini açar.

basis: a victory hymn directed to God
note: The commentary says a beneficiary answers good with public praise; after Israel's deliverance Judith begins a song to her God with instruments.

basis: singing a new song for God's strength
note: The commentary describes praise that tells the giver's deeds; Judith sings a new song to God and praises his greatness and invincible power.

basis: do not add reproach to a gift
note: The commentary describes hamd's reverse as rubbing one's favor in another's face; Ben Sira directly says not to add reproach or hurtful words when doing good or giving.
Ben Sira, iyi işe azarlama katmamayı ve armağanı kırıcı sözle bozmamayı buyurur; yorumdaki yetehammedü aleyye sahnesinin açık etik karşıtıdır.
The commentary warns that the recipient can be humiliated by a favor held over them; Ben Sira says a gift from a grudging person dims the eyes, showing how manner changes the gift.
Budalanın az verip çok azarladığı armağan, nimeti alıcının başına kakan kişi için en yakın Yahudi hikmet sahnesidir.

basis: bless God for all his works
note: The commentary makes praise the recipient's answer to God's favor; Ben Sira blesses the God who does great things everywhere and asks that God grant joy of heart.

basis: command to declare God's deeds to the living
note: The commentary says the recipient should tell others about the giver's favor; Raphael tells Tobit and Tobias to bless God, give thanks, and declare God's works before all the living.
Refael, Tanrı'yı bereketlemeyi, onun kendileri için yaptıklarını yaşayanların önünde tanımayı ve işlerini herkese duyurmayı buyurur; 93:11'in Yahudi anlatı karşılığıdır.

basis: declare God's greatness among the nations
note: The commentary says God's favor should be told to others; Tobit calls Israel to declare God's greatness before the nations and praise him in Jerusalem.
The commentary joins received mercy with a public response; Tobit says those who turn to God with their whole heart will bless him in truth.

note: The commentary joins received provision to praise; in the same psalm's assembly the poor eat and are satisfied, and those seeking God praise him.
The commentary names Rabb as the one completing good and making the recipient's way possible; the psalm calls YHWH shepherd and says the speaker lacks nothing.
The commentary calls the bestowed favor a path-gift; the shepherd psalm says God restores the soul and leads the speaker in right paths.
Canı yenileyip doğruluk yollarında yürütmesi, nimeti iyileştirme ile yol gösterme olarak birleştirir.
İyilik ve sadık sevginin bütün günler takip etmesi ve YHWH'nin evinde oturma, rahmet, yol ve kutsal evin varışta birleştiği bir mezmur sonudur.

basis: all paths are love and faithfulness
note: The commentary joins divine favor to the path; the psalm says all YHWH's paths are steadfast love and faithfulness for those who keep his covenant.

basis: asking to be shown God's ways
note: The commentary calls the bestowed favor a path-gift; the psalmist asks God to make his ways known.
The commentary says the gift is completed by walking the path; the psalm asks God to lead and teach the speaker because God is his salvation.
Dua eden, YHWH'nin yollarını kendisine bildirmesini ve patikalarını öğretmesini ister; ihdinâ sırâtal-müstakîm'in yalvarış biçimine yakındır.
YHWH'den hakikatte yöneltmesini ve öğretmesini istemek, yolun yalnız yön değil ilahi eğitim olarak da verilen nimet oluşunu açar.

basis: yol öğretmek ve düz patikada götürmek
note: YHWH'nin yolunu öğretmesi ve düşmanlar yüzünden düz patikada götürmesi için dua, sırât-ı müstakîm isteğinin yakın mezmur paralelidir.

The commentary says the recipient's praise returns at the journey's end; after God turns mourning into dancing, the psalmist says his soul will sing praise and give thanks forever. (Hebrew WLC numbering.)
The commentary distinguishes recounting God's favors from boasting in one's own giving; the psalmist's soul boasts in YHWH, so the humble hear and rejoice.
The commentary makes praise the recipient's response; the psalmist magnifies YHWH and reports that God answered and delivered him from fear.
The commentary says God's favors are recounted before others; the psalmist does not hide God's deliverance, faithfulness, and love from the great congregation. (Hebrew WLC numbering.)

The commentary's account of hamd includes telling another person the giver's goodness; this verse says the speaker has not concealed God's steadfast love and faithfulness from the assembly. (Hebrew WLC numbering.)
Mezmur Tanrı'yı “benim için tamamlayan” diye çağırır; Rabbin nimeti sonuna kadar götürmesi iddiasına doğrudan tamamlanma dili verir.
The commentary's hamd includes telling others about the giver's favors; the psalmist invites God-fearers to hear what God did for him.
Tanrı'dan korkanları dinlemeye çağırıp canına ne yaptığını anlatır; alıcının kendi nimetini topluluğa aktarmasıdır.

basis: blessing that makes God's way known
note: The commentary joins a bestowed favor to a path; the psalm asks God to bless the people so that God's way and saving power become known on earth. (Hebrew WLC numbering.)

basis: nations rejoice under God's just guidance
note: The commentary asks for a path of divine favor; the psalm calls the nations to rejoice because God judges peoples with equity and guides the nations on earth. (Hebrew WLC numbering.)

basis: blessing that reaches the ends of the earth
note: The commentary describes a community receiving favor; the psalm asks God to bless Israel so that all the ends of the earth fear him. (Hebrew WLC numbering.)

basis: he people receive provision from heaven
note: The commentary describes favor as good conveyed to a recipient; the psalm says God opened heaven and rained manna to feed Israel.

basis: the people remain ungrateful after wonders
note: The commentary makes praise the fitting response to received benefits; despite God's wonders, the people continue to sin and fail to trust.
The commentary distinguishes divine mercy from anger; the psalm says God is compassionate, forgives, and often turns away his anger from the people.
The commentary calls the received favor a path-gift; pilgrims crossing the Valley of Baca make it a spring, and the early rain covers it with blessings. (Hebrew WLC numbering.)

basis: God's love and faithfulness told for generations
note: The commentary says the benefactor's good is told aloud; the psalmist says he will sing of YHWH's steadfast love and make his faithfulness known through every generation. (Hebrew WLC numbering.)
Mezmurcu bütün yüreğiyle YHWH'ye şükreder ve bütün harikalarını anlatır; hamdin verenin iyiliklerini başkalarının yanında sayması oluşuna yakındır.

İbr. נֹעַם, hoşluk veya lütuf için N-ʿ-M ailesinin bir kullanımıdır; dua onu işimizin eserini sağlamlaştırmasıyla birleştirir ve yorumdaki iyi hâl ile nimetin tamamlanmasına ihtiyatlı dilsel köprü kurar.

basis: hearts that stray and do not know God's ways
note: The commentary distinguishes those who receive guidance from those who stray; the psalm identifies the wilderness generation by their wandering hearts and failure to know God's ways.

basis: divine anger and exclusion from rest
note: The commentary names those under anger as the contrary group; the psalm's wilderness oracle ends with God's oath that they will not enter his rest.
Tapınma çağrısı, hemen sonraki ayetin onun eli altındaki halk tasviriyle birlikte, sağlayıcıya kulluk cevabını verir.

basis: otlağının halkı ve eli altındaki koyunlar
note: Halkın onun otlağı ve eli altındaki koyunlar oluşu, 95:6'daki kulluğu koruyan ve besleyen Rabbe cevap olarak temellendirir.

basis: the delivered people bless God's holy name
note: The commentary makes praise follow received deliverance; Wisdom says the righteous sang praise and blessed God's holy name after their rescue.
The commentary says God's favor includes the capacity to praise; Wisdom says the divine Wisdom opened the mouths of the mute and made the tongues of infants clear.

basis: we strayed from the way of truth
note: The commentary contrasts the sought path with those who stray; the wicked in Wisdom confess that they left the way of truth and righteousness.
The commentary excludes those who lose the way; the same confession says the wicked wearied themselves on paths of lawlessness, giving the wandering a moral setting.

basis: blessing before benefiting from the world
note: The commentary says hamd answers a received favor; the rabbis rule that one may not enjoy worldly benefit without a blessing, making praise a recognition of God's ownership and gift.

basis: food blessings traced to manna and land
note: The commentary places praise after a received benefit; the rabbis attribute the blessings after meals to Moses at the manna, Joshua on entering the land, and David and Solomon at Jerusalem, reading Israel's liturgy through successive gifts.

basis: Moses' mercy attributes become a repeated prayer form
note: The commentary repeats the mercy formula in 1:1 and 1:3; the rabbis read Exodus 34:6 as the order of divine attributes Moses was taught to invoke whenever Israel sins and seeks forgiveness.

basis: giving from what belongs to God
note: The commentary depicts the giver's good passing to a recipient; Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah says to give God what is God's, since the person and possessions are God's, interpreting David's words in 1 Chronicles 29:14.

basis: blessing God for adversity as well as good
note: The commentary says hamd is broader than thanks for a discrete favor; the Mishnah requires a blessing for bad events as for good, extending praise beyond a favorable outcome.
